end.summary:
Practised interpreting position-time and velocity-time graphs as motion stories.
Read x-t slope as velocity and v-t slope as acceleration.
Correctly calculated velocity as 3 m/s and displacement from graph areas, including 120 m and 16 m.
Identified flat x-t sections as rest and flat v-t sections as constant speed.
Initially described an x-t graph as a path picture, then corrected this during the lesson.
end.parentNote: Ira practised reading graphs as motion stories rather than pictures of the road. They used slope for velocity or acceleration and area under a velocity-time graph for distance, including the 120 m and 16 m examples. The path-picture mix-up was corrected later by explaining that an x-t graph shows position changing with time (turns 8–10). At home, ask Ira to describe one x-t and one v-t graph aloud, naming what each flat or sloping section means.
